title: C# Async Programming: Task, async/await & Cancellation
description: Master asynchronous C#: what async/await actually do, running work concurrently with Task.WhenAll and Task.WhenAny, cancelling long-running operations with CancellationToken, handling exceptions across async code, and streaming results with IAsyncEnumerable.

lessons.title: Introduction to Asynchronous Programming

questions.prompt: What does await do to the method it is used in?
options: Blocks the calling thread until the operation finishes
Pauses the method without blocking the thread, resuming when the operation completes
Runs the method on a new process
questions.answer: Pauses the method without blocking the thread, resuming when the operation completes

questions.prompt: A ____<T> represents asynchronous work that will eventually produce a value of type T.
Blocking the main thread in a desktop app can freeze the UI.

lessons.title: async and await

questions.prompt: What does marking a method async actually do?
options: Runs it on a background thread automatically
Enables the use of await inside that method
questions.answer: Enables the use of await inside that method

questions.prompt: Task.____(1000) asynchronously waits about a second without blocking the thread, unlike Thread.Sleep.
Calling .Result on a Task instead of awaiting it can cause a deadlock in some applications.

lessons.title: Task.WhenAll and Task.WhenAny

questions.prompt: What does Task.WhenAll(t1, t2, t3) do?
options: Runs the tasks one after another
Waits for all three tasks to complete, running them concurrently
Returns as soon as the first task finishes
questions.answer: Waits for all three tasks to complete, running them concurrently

questions.prompt: Task.____ resolves as soon as the first of several tasks finishes, useful for timeout patterns.
Calling an async method without awaiting it immediately starts the work in the background.

lessons.title: Cancellation with CancellationToken

questions.prompt: What is responsible for actually triggering a cancellation?
token.____() throws an OperationCanceledException if cancellation has been requested.
A CancellationToken can itself cancel work, without needing a CancellationTokenSource.

lessons.title: Exception Handling in Async Code

questions.prompt: Where does an exception thrown inside an awaited async method surface?
options: At the await point, just like a normal synchronous call
Only in a background log file
It always crashes the whole application immediately
questions.answer: At the await point, just like a normal synchronous call

questions.prompt: An exception thrown inside an async ____ method cannot be caught by a surrounding try/catch.
When multiple tasks passed to Task.WhenAll fail, only the first exception is rethrown by the await, though the rest remain available on each Task.

lessons.title: Async Streams with IAsyncEnumerable

options: A single value that resolves in the future
A sequence whose items may each take time to produce
A synchronous collection with no delays
A type only usable inside Unity
questions.answer: A sequence whose items may each take time to produce

questions.prompt: ____ foreach consumes an IAsyncEnumerable<T>, awaiting each item as it becomes available.
An async IAsyncEnumerable<T> method can use yield return, just like a synchronous iterator.

lessons.title: Final Project: Async Multi-Source Downloader
lessons.content:
# Final Project: Async Multi-Source Downloader

Combine everything from this course into a small but realistic async tool.

## Requirements

1. Write an async method that downloads or fetches data from at least 3 different sources (URLs, files, or simulated delays with `Task.Delay`) **concurrently**, using `Task.WhenAll`.
2. Support cancellation: accept a `CancellationToken`, and let the user cancel the whole operation (e.g. by pressing a key while it's running).
3. Handle failures gracefully: if one source fails, log which one and continue reporting results for the others, instead of the whole program crashing.
4. Add a timeout using `Task.WhenAny` racing the real operation against `Task.Delay(timeout)`, cancelling and reporting a timeout message if the delay wins.
5. Use an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` method to stream and print progress updates (e.g. "Source A: 50% done") as they happen, instead of only printing a final summary.

## Stretch goals

- Add retry logic: if a source fails, retry it up to 2 more times with a short delay between attempts before giving up.
- Track and print total elapsed time, and compare it to what sequential (non-concurrent) execution would have taken.
- Wrap the whole thing in a small console menu so a user can re-run it with different sources without restarting the program.

Submit your repository link below when you are done, an instructor will review it before you can mark this lesson complete. Good luck! 🚀
